misconceptions.description: Writing a problem statement that names a desired solution or a vague symptom instead of the evidenced gap and its source of demand
misconceptions.trigger: problem statement says make it interesting or needs a refresh rather than locating the observable failure point
misconceptions.feedback: State the learner segment, the observable failure point, and the source of demand before any solution. The fix is not the problem.

misconceptions.description: Building a learner profile from praise adjectives that do not constrain any design decision
misconceptions.trigger: profile lists motivated, tech-savvy, or eager without design-relevant variability
misconceptions.feedback: Keep only attributes that would change a frame: prior knowledge, access conditions, task context. Drop adjectives that change nothing.

misconceptions.description: Accepting an AI-generated persona as verified learner data instead of a hypothesis to confirm
misconceptions.trigger: learner pastes AI demographics into the packet without checking intake or context evidence
misconceptions.feedback: Treat AI personas as candidate attributes. Confirm each against real intake or context data and reject fabricated ones.

misconceptions.description: Setting a problem goal that cannot be tested by a later revision
misconceptions.trigger: goal says improve or enhance with no measurable learner action or target
misconceptions.feedback: Tie the goal to a measurable learner action so a later storyboard revision can be evaluated against it.
